frozen_contract.information: current frame/page/pool owner, current target config, existing map/state and paid history; no future CQ/reuse truth
frozen_contract.external_work: same arrival/route/consumer/valid completion/service; each policy derives actual allocation/recycle
frozen_contract.copy_fallback: if used, explicit acceptance responsibility and copy pool/bandwidth accounting required
frozen_contract.hardware_DMA_drain: root-owned source review; no claim proven by this seat

events.allocation_index: no new record merely because packet changes
events.lock_context: existing pool cache/ring context; record stays live

events.design: While frame is valid, sparse lookup; reserve K record and publish unique CREATING in source and target indexes before external map; map full authorized granule with same DMA backend; recheck target gate and record state before LIVE
events.allocation_index: record and nodes pre-reserved; K full or CREATING contention uses O0 without waiting; later admission retry allowed
events.lock_context: short bucket/record lock for claims, no spinlock across unknown DMA API; target CPU read-side/config lifetime held
events.responsible: unique creator; close handoff owns any completed private mapping
events.evidence_limit: M08 proves proposed RFC atomic mapping pattern, not this adaptation or selected backend latency

events.design: Read mapping readiness/address and compute packet offset; prescribed per-use DMA sync; G token_get under LIVE check, N no extra token under narrower lifetime proof
events.allocation_index: sparse lookup or paid direct table; fixed B simplifies key only
events.lock_context: G close/token serialization; N CPU reader/publication protocol still required

events.design: Accepted prefix transfers original frame responsibility; G mode/xdpf/handle uses three logical entries; N completion requires mode/xdpf only or compatible third entry
events.allocation_index: existing FIFO storage pattern; no mandatory fourth entry
events.lock_context: existing SQ submission ownership plus correct new mode

events.design: Release G token/private resources on failure; unpublished map creator cleans once; cached published map may remain; original frame stays with rejected suffix responsibility; N has no token rollback
events.allocation_index: failed slot/index erase obeys CPU grace before record reuse
events.lock_context: no wait for creator; failed close handoff explicit
events.responsible: creator or unique closer; original suffix owner returns frame

events.design: G token_put before xdp_return_frame_bulk; N no token/handle lookup and no record use after frame return; O0 retains ordinary unmap; stop cleanup uses same mode obligations only after true DMA drain
events.lock_context: existing XDP return RCU constraint; cannot wait for own source close

events.design: G LIVE->CLOSING blocks new token, remain discoverable, unmap once after active users finish; N forbids independent idle eviction
events.allocation_index: record retained until all indexes/CPU readers/closer obligations end
events.lock_context: short state claim; no wait for DMA under spinlock or same NAPI
events.evidence_limit: RFC unmap_all clearing bit before actual unmap is not a standalone admission gate

events.design: Unified hook before A DMA release/release_cnt/clear_pp_info/put_page; absent sparse record continues stock; otherwise EXITING blocks map, closes all discoverable bindings, completes unmap/sync, then one-shot original finalizer
events.allocation_index: source index lookup; active closer record cannot disappear early
events.lock_context: last-fragment gate supplies no legitimate per-page active DMA under N; backend may still require Q; source hook cannot spin waiting target closer while in its waited RCU read-side
events.responsible: source release transaction and unique unmapper

events.design: Caller first stops allocation; cached/ring pages hit unified hook; in-flight frame/fragments return later; record/pool_ctx follows page inflight until release count, not only pool disconnect
events.allocation_index: pool_ctx and outstanding record/Q accounting live until final pages exit
events.lock_context: do not unmap active page solely because pool destroy called

events.design: Close target admission, drain map/submit CPU readers before claiming bindings, perform real SQ/device DMA drain and frame cleanup, uniquely unmap/forget live slots, then retire config/index epoch
events.allocation_index: enumerate LIVE and CREATING records and retired Q records; no index reuse before old references disappear
events.lock_context: target control outer, page short lock inner; do not hold owner lock waiting target; source Q if necessary to avoid read-side/closer cycle
events.evidence_limit: RCU/SRCU/network-reader synchronization does not certify hardware DMA drain; actual FW semantics unverified here

events.design: Same valid DMA backend and aligned actual basepage granule already have single/page unmap frontend precedent in stock B CQ and source return; absent new wait/close contention, synchronous release-hook B unmap is a conditional executable branch; only where actual context and service costs remain acceptable
events.allocation_index: preexisting record/close metadata; no surprise blocking allocation
events.lock_context: outside source spinlock; last pp-ref does not prove DMA API context support
events.evidence_limit: Single map/unmap frontends delegate to page frontends in saved v6.12; this supports stable-target synchronous branch, not every backend, hardware/latency, or target-close race. RFC process-context unmap is not by itself a proof the ordinary adaptation must defer.

events.design: Defer actual source exit, not just final put; keep source page, inflight, pool_ctx and target config alive; embedded retire node queues worker; worker completes unmap/sync, indexes/CPU grace and exactly one stock finalizer
events.allocation_index: retire node/worker resources reserved at admission; Q worst-case covers all K mapped pages simultaneously; K full stops new persistent admission via O0
events.lock_context: no blocking source read-side; worker outside softirq; one-shot bypass prevents recursive hook
events.time_bound: unknown absent bounded backend/driver service; count cap not a time guarantee

narrow_token_proof.type: conditional source-bound reasoning, not executed concurrency proof
necessary_conditions: every prepare and accepted transfer holds original frame/all page_pool fragment responsibility until CQ or legal device drain
source exit only through unified true-release hook after last fragment and driver bias drained
no independent map eviction, source revoke, migration or rights/config change without explicit equivalent drain
target unmap occurs only after admission closure, current creator/submit CPU readers drain and real DMA drain
CPU metadata/config lifetime and unique closer still enforced
narrow_token_proof.sufficiency_scope: Those conditions let existing frame references protect active DMA against source exit; independent binding active counter duplicates this obligation and can be removed for V1_N and R_OB4K_T_N
does_not_imply: single buffer equals one page per packet
all unmap can run in NAPI
failure_neighbors: independent idle eviction while another same-page fragment is DMA or current frame is preparing
target config changes before gate+reader+DMA drain
frame returned before last binding metadata access
target claims binding then waits RCU while source in that RCU waits binding closer

metadata_RAM: K sparse records and hash buckets
pre-reserved work and delayed record reuse
resource_accounting.page_table_RAM: ordinary leaf/supporting page allocation separately measured; no PMD coverage credit
resource_accounting.IOVA: virtual aperture separately; per-page DMA allocation vs full affine window not RAM
resource_accounting.physical_payload: bytes of actual S union P union C union Q, de-duplicated; source-owned Q may overlap S
resource_accounting.P_note: N has no idle cache page/pp pin; P can be zero while Q nonzero
resource_accounting.feedback: derive policy-specific actual allocation/recycle, source replacement pages and map reuse; never enforce identical PFN sequence
resource_accounting.bandwidth_and_completion: copy bytes, actual useful completion, rejection/fallback and service delay reported separately

decisive_prediction.if: legal T, fixed target epoch, no independent eviction, all actual frame/fragment references held until CQ/drain, and synchronous/Q exit contract closes
decisive_prediction.then: actual reuse of same source-generation page can reuse B mapping across ordinary recycle with no idle get_page/pp_ref and no per-TX binding token; source exit unmaps first; no mandatory fourth FIFO logical entry
decisive_prediction.adjacent_failure: add independent map eviction without active-use accounting/drain and another same-page fragment/prepare can lose mapping
decisive_prediction.interpretation: capability feasibility prediction, not measured CPU/RAM benefit or independent mechanism proof

root_unresolved: accept real target gate/CPU reader/DMA drain/config lifetime contract
selected backend actual synchronous retire or Q service costs
if less metadata read claimed, fix concrete equal-cost side table or transfer representation

minimal_next_evidence.input: One named workload/backend with real source epoch/page join/alloc/recycle/exit, B map/accept/CQ/target-close events, and attributable O0 map/unmap CPU costs; reuse existing raw evidence first; missing inputs stay missing
minimal_next_evidence.advance_if: Actual repeated B mappings within source generations leave meaningful avoidable CPU opportunity under finite K and observed retirement/Q/service conditions; advance ordinary integration value assessment only
minimal_next_evidence.restrict_if: Mostly single B use before real source exit, small avoidable mapping CPU, or service/resource contract fails; restrict named deployment/version only
minimal_next_evidence.does_not_prove: V1 novelty or net benefit from opportunities alone; no automatic driver/collector/model/board work
